title: Jeff Regan, Investigator
paragraphs: A hard-boiled private-eye series about Jeff Regan, an investigator working for a detective agency and handling murder, blackmail, missing persons, and other cases in postwar Los Angeles.
Regional CBS West Coast private-eye drama created by E. Jack Neuman.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Jack Webb first run (July 10, 1948 to December 18, 1948) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]] and Frank Graham / Paul Dubov revival (October 5, 1949 to September 3, 1950) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Sterling Tracy (producer, director, and transcriber), Bob Stevenson (announcer), Richard Aurandt (organist, music, and composer), Frank Nelson (performer), [[person|jack-webb|Jack Webb]] (performer), E. Jack Neuman (writer), and Frank Graham (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]] and [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

The stories often return to murder and homicide, fraud, theft and confidence schemes, missing persons and disappearance, Los Angeles and Southern California, police, detectives and investigation, and blackmail, extortion and threats.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar private-eye boom, Regional network production, 1949 revival softens the lead, and Military rebroadcast preservation.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|richard-diamond-private-detective|Richard Diamond, Private Detective]], and [[show|escape|Escape]].
